thread:
anya (PM): Heads-up — large customer (HealthCo) just asked for a contract-level priority queue + burst SLA for their Dedicated pool. They want 6-week turnaround and a pricing add-on. Need to decide if this becomes a productized "priority add-on" or a custom contract clause. Thoughts?

sam (Sales): This is a named-account request, >$1.2M ARR if we commit. They want guaranteed priority during peak batches (batch windows, not continuous). Can push for add-on pricing but they’ll want hard language in the SOW.

leo (Finance): From unit-econ POV we need a clear billing shape. If we do guaranteed priority we must price for reserved headroom + wasted capacity risk. Suggest model: baseline reserved + "priority credits" consumed when queued bursts exceed baseline.

marta (Legal): Any SLA in contract needs clear definitions: what exactly counts as "priority", measurement windows, remedies (credits capped), termination triggers. Also watch for language implying 100% availability — we should prefer "best-effort priority" with measurable metrics.

devin (Eng): Implementation note: runtime-level queueing + policy routing required. We already have routing policies by region/tier, but we don't have per-contract queue tokens. Work involved: API (quota tokens), router change for priority lanes, and dashboard telemetry. Estimate ~3 wks eng effort + 1 wk QA for a minimal prototype. Risk: latency for non-priority customers could spike unless we cap admission.

nora (Solutions): HealthCo intends to run nightly batch scoring windows (2h) where they need fast tail latency. They can tolerate preemption outside windows. Our priority model could be time-windowed to reduce continuous cost. They prefer explicit token buckets tied to contract.

anya (PM): OK — sounds like a product add-on is plausible. Drafting some candidate launch criteria for discussion:
- Clear SLA metrics: 95th/99th tail for queued requests + measurement method
- Billing model: token-based or per-minute priority premium defined in pricing sheet
- Ops tooling: per-contract telemetry (latency, queue depth), alerting, and incident playbook
- Legal: contract clause template + credit cap and audit requirements
- Engineering: prototype + canary rollout plan + fallback behavior defined

sam (Sales): For pricing band, propose +30% on top of reserved capacity for token bucket + $X per 10k priority-tokens consumed. We can negotiate sliding scale for multi-year commits.

leo (Finance): +30% might be too blunt. Suggest we model at token price such that expected incremental margin >= 40% after accounting for headroom. I'll run a quick P&L sensitivity vs burst frequency.

devin (Eng): Prototype idea — expose a contract field: "priority_tokens": 1000 and a routing flag. Minimal config example:
```
contract_id: HC-2026-01
priority: "burst"
priority_tokens: 1000
time_windows:
  - start: "02:00"
    end: "04:00"
fallback_policy: "standard"
```
We can wire this to router and track token consumption.

marta (Legal): Draft language bits we need in SOW: definition of priority, measurement window, remedies (credit calculation), force majeure, audit rights. Avoid SLA with monetary penalty exposure beyond capped credits. Also need data residency attestation for Dedicated.

nora (Solutions): On deployment side, recommend we offer an onboarding checklist for customers: expected traffic profile, representative payloads, test runs, and a pre-cutover dry-run to tune token sizing.

anya (PM): Good. Proposed launch criteria checklist (must-haves):
- SLA doc + measurement spec OKed by Legal
- Pricing model signed off by Finance (token pricing + minimum commit)
- Eng prototype validated in staging with tail-latency targets met in 2 dry-runs
- Console telemetry and billing meter implemented
- Customer onboarding plan + runbook

sam (Sales): If we can hit those in ~6 weeks we can include this in HealthCo's SOW. I'll push for the minimum commit to be 12 months.

leo (Finance): I'll produce 2 models by Friday: conservative/high-availability cost and a revenue-first discount curve. Need expected burst frequency from Solutions to size headroom.

devin (Eng): Putting a small spike risk flag: if multiple customers use priority simultaneously, we need admission control. Suggest global soft-headroom and automatic fallback to compatible model variants. Canary rollout: one region, limited contracts, monitor 1 week.

marta (Legal): I'll draft clause template and an exhibit that limits credits & clarifies measurement. ETA 5 business days.

anya (PM): Actions and owners:
- devin (Eng) -> prototype + staging runs (owner), due in 3w
- leo (Finance) -> pricing models and margin analysis, due Fri
- marta (Legal) -> SLA clause draft, due +5 business days
- sam (Sales) -> negotiate minimum commit and timeline with HealthCo, keep product looped, due this week
- nora (Solutions) -> collect burst profile & runbook inputs, due +4 days

nora (Solutions): Ack. I'll send the customer traffic CSV and example payloads in a DM.

devin (Eng): ack, starting spike emulator tests tomorrow.

leo (Finance): ack, will share models in #finance when done.

marta (Legal): ack, will drop a draft in this thread for visibility.

anya (PM): Great — let's sync on Monday 11am for a quick triage. If anyone spots a hard blocker call it out now.

sam (Sales): +1 for Mon 11. One ask: can we include a non-binding estimated list price to show HealthCo during negotiation? Even a placeholder helps.

leo (Finance): Will include a placeholder price band in my models.

anya (PM): Nice. Closing notes: prefer productized "priority add-on" vs bespoke SOW unless customer demands exclusivity. That keeps it scalable. :thumbsup: 

sam (Sales): :thumbsup:
